name: Óðrœrir
aliases: The Kettle of the Mead of Poetry
powers: Holds the mead of poetry; whoever drinks it gains poetry and wisdom.
description: The kettle that holds the mead of poetry, brewed by the dwarves Fjalar and Galar from the blood of Kvasir, the wisest of beings, mixed with honey. Whoever drinks from Óðrœrir gains the gift of poetry and wisdom. Odin stole the mead from the giant Suttungr, drained the vessels Boðn and Són and the kettle itself, and shared it with the Æsir, keeping a small part for poets.

name: Óttastafur
powers: Strikes fear into those against whom it is used.
description: Óttastafur, the fear stave of the Huld manuscript, drawn to strike fear into others. As a weapon of psychological magic it was meant to cow rivals or enemies without a blow. It is one of the aggressive galdrastafir recorded beside the protective and luck-giving signs, showing that the stave tradition served harm as readily as help.

name: The Offer Stone
powers: Cups held offerings for blessing and healing.
description: The offer stone (offersten), a boulder with cup-shaped hollows where offerings were made. Hundreds of such stones survive across Sweden, often beside churches, springs, or old cult sites; small gifts of coins, food, or tar were placed in the cups, and in later Christian times the stones were avoided or 'baptised'. The cup-marked stones are counted among Sweden's oldest cult objects.
source: Swedish antiquarian and ethnological records of offer stones

name: Oseberg Ship
description: The richly carved oak vessel of a Viking-age ship burial uncovered at the Oseberg farm near Tønsberg, Norway, in 1904. About 21.8 meters long, the ship carried two women and rich grave goods, including the carved Oseberg wagon and sledges. Its animal-head prow and decorated frames show the craft of early 9th-century Norse shipbuilding, and it is exhibited in the Viking Ship Museum in Oslo.

name: Lyre of Orpheus
maker: Gift of Apollo or Hermes to Orpheus
powers: Charmed beasts, trees, and stones; moved the dead and soothed Cerberus.
description: The lyre of Orpheus, a gift from Apollo or Hermes with the power to charm beasts, trees, and stones and to move the dead; its music soothed Cerberus and won Hades' consent to let Eurydice return, a bargain lost when Orpheus looked back. After his death the lyre was set among the stars.

name: Bow of Odysseus
material: Polished wood with horn tip (gift of Iphitus)
maker: Given to Odysseus by Iphitus; strung only by its owner
powers: Shot an arrow through twelve axe heads; brought death to the suitors of Ithaca.
description: The great bow of Odysseus, which he alone could string and shoot through twelve axe-heads; Penelope's contest of the bow is the test of her suitors, and Odysseus slays them with it on his return to Ithaca in the Odyssey. Its unyielding strength stands for the hero's unchallenged identity.

name: Oni no Kanabo
powers: Said to crush any demon or mortal it strikes
description: The iron-studded club that Japanese tales and art place in the grip of the oni, the red-and-blue ogre of legend. Treated as a stock attribute of the ogre rather than a documented artifact, it appears in tales from Shuten-doji onward, its weight said to crush whatever it strikes; no historical example survives.
